title: Sing Buri 2-Day Itinerary — Old Temples + Mae La Fish
metaDesc: A relaxed 2-day, 1-night Sing Buri itinerary in Thailand: the giant Reclining Buddha, Wat Phikun Thong, the Bang Rachan battlefield, then grilled Mae La snakehead fish by the river.
keywords: Sing Buri 2 day itinerary, Sing Buri trip plan, Mae La snakehead fish, Wat Phra Non Chaksi, Bang Rachan camp
intro: Sing Buri is a small town less than two hours' drive from Bangkok, which makes it a good unhurried weekend trip. You can pay respects at a huge Reclining Buddha, follow the story of the Bang Rachan defenders, and finish with grilled Mae La snakehead fish by the river — the dish the province is known for. Here's a 2-day, 1-night route that fills the days well and keeps you fed.

blocks.html: Sing Buri sits about 140 kilometers from Bangkok. Take the Asia Highway (Route 32) and you'll be there in roughly an hour and a half to two hours. The town itself is small, and the main temples and sights aren't far apart, so two days and one night is about right with no need to rush. Day one focuses on temples and history; day two is markets, a café stop, and grilled Mae La snakehead fish before you head home.

blocks.text: Day One — Reclining Buddha and the Bang Rachan Trail

items.activity: Leave Bangkok, drive the Asia Highway toward Sing Buri
items.note: Stop at a gas station or grab breakfast on the way. You'll reach Sing Buri around 10am.
The 47-meter Reclining Buddha is one of the largest in Thailand, and this is a royal temple. There's a small market out front worth a quick look.

items.activity: Wat Phikun Thong — pay respects to Luang Pho Yai
items.note: Phra Phuttha Suwan Mongkon Maha Muni, a huge seated Buddha in the blessing posture, sits by the Noi River, about 9 kilometers from the Reclining Buddha temple.
Try Sing Buri's well-known boat noodles, or a made-to-order shop in town works too.
Learn about the Bang Rachan villagers who banded together and held out for months in the late Ayutthaya period. There are dioramas and history panels to read.

items.activity: Wat Pho Kao Ton (Wat Mai Daeng)
items.note: Close to the Bang Rachan site, this old Ayutthaya-era temple is tied to the heroes' story. A short walk-through is enough.

items.activity: Check in to your hotel in town and rest
items.note: Sing Buri has small, affordable hotels and resorts in town that are easy to get around from.

items.activity: Dinner by the Chao Phraya River
items.note: There are several riverside restaurants in town with a relaxed feel. Try the river fish or river prawns.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Wat Phikun Thong, Wat Phra Non Chaksi, and the Bang Rachan site are on different sides of town. Plan a single loop — start with the temple nearest the town entrance and work your way out — to cut down on driving time.

blocks.text: Day Two — Markets, a Café, Then Mae La Fish

items.note: There are early-morning coffee shops in town, or you can eat at your hotel.

items.activity: Wat Sawang Arom — watch Buddha image casting and the Nang Yai museum
items.note: This temple is known for casting Buddha images, a craft passed down from Thonburi-era founders, and it has a Nang Yai (giant shadow puppet) museum. The museum is open Mon–Fri 9am–4pm and Sat–Sun 8:30am–5pm.
Sing Buri has several newer cafés around town and near the Bang Rachan site. Sit down for a coffee before lunch.

items.activity: Lunch — grilled Mae La snakehead fish by the river
items.note: The highlight of the trip. The grilled Mae La snakehead spots are along the Mae La waterway in Inthar Buri district. The fish is sweet and fresh, salt-grilled and fragrant, served with two dipping sauces.

items.activity: Pick up souvenirs to take home
items.note: Sun-dried Mae La snakehead, processed snakehead products, and snakehead-fish chili paste are sold at the riverside shops and town markets.
You'll be home before evening, no rush.

blocks.text: Where to Eat Mae La Snakehead Fish

blocks.html: Mae La snakehead is the snakehead fish raised and caught in the Mae La waterway in Inthar Buri district. It's known for firmer flesh and a sweeter taste than ordinary snakehead. The popular restaurants cluster along the Mae La waterway, and the go-to dish is salt-grilled snakehead, split down the middle and dipped in sweet fish sauce or seafood sauce. Here are the spots people stop at most often.

items.name: Mae La Pla Phao
items.blurb: A much-talked-about grilled Mae La snakehead spot. The fish is fresh and sweet with a smoky aroma, served with two kinds of dipping sauce. The dining area is roomy and comfortable to sit in.
items.meta: Bang Man subdistrict, Mueang Sing Buri · about ฿100–250/person

items.name: Rim Mae La Ton Tamrap
items.blurb: A long-established spot, decades old, on the Mae La waterway. Known for snakehead grilled over a neem-branch fire, with a relaxed riverside feel.

items.name: Baan Suan Mae La Ka Long
items.blurb: Set among big garden trees with several seating zones, including a riverside one. The standout is grilled Mae La snakehead with sweet fish sauce. A great pick for families.
items.meta: Mae La subdistrict, Inthar Buri district · about ฿150–300/person

items.name: Rot Nueng Sun-Dried Mae La Snakehead
items.blurb: If you want to take some home, this place makes proper sun-dried Mae La snakehead — firm flesh that fries up nicely at home. It's the souvenir Sing Buri locals recommend.
items.meta: Nam Tan subdistrict, Inthar Buri district · souvenir to take home

blocks.text: What to Know Before You Go to Sing Buri

items: A car is by far the easiest — the sights are spread out beyond town and public transport within the province is limited. Driving yourself or renting a car is much smoother.
Temples open early — most temples are open from morning to evening. Go in the morning when the sun is gentler and there are fewer people.
Mae La fish is best at lunch — the grill spots turn over fish quickly at midday, so it's fresher than at other meals.
Allow time for driving around town — the temples are roughly 9–15 kilometers apart, so build in travel time and don't pack the schedule too tightly.

faq.q: What should I do in Sing Buri in 2 days and 1 night?
faq.a: Day one: pay respects at the Reclining Buddha (Wat Phra Non Chaksi) and Luang Pho Yai at Wat Phikun Thong, then visit the Bang Rachan Heroes Monument and Wat Pho Kao Ton. Day two: stop by Wat Sawang Arom, have coffee at a riverside café, and finish with grilled Mae La snakehead before heading home.

faq.q: Where can I eat Mae La snakehead fish in Sing Buri?
faq.a: Most grilled Mae La snakehead spots are along the Mae La waterway, in Inthar Buri and Mueang districts. Popular ones include Mae La Pla Phao, Rim Mae La Ton Tamrap, and Baan Suan Mae La Ka Long. The fish is freshest at lunch.

faq.q: Is Sing Buri a long drive from Bangkok?
faq.a: Not far — it's about 140 kilometers from Bangkok. Take the Asia Highway (Route 32) and it's roughly an hour and a half to two hours. It works well as a weekend day trip or a single overnight.

faq.q: What is Sing Buri's signature souvenir?
faq.a: Sun-dried Mae La snakehead is the first thing that comes to mind. There are also processed snakehead products, snakehead-fish chili paste, and grilled Mae La snakehead to take home. You'll find them at the Mae La riverside shops and town markets.
